status: research-informed candidate taxonomy; not empirically validated as a scoring instrument
changelog: v0.2.0: Expanded taxonomy from 24 to 26 patterns by adding L07 (Mechanical punctuation habits and em-dash overuse) and L08 (Predictable paragraph architecture and list-like flows). Updated L04 burstiness guidance and evidence level to be descriptive and advisory rather than prescriptive word-count bins. Added explicit scientific precedence exceptions for study design, methodological sequencing, hypothesis enumeration, and standardized reporting conventions across L04, L07, and L08.

priority_definitions.P0: meaning, integrity or demonstrable discourse defect; review first
priority_definitions.P2: lower-priority stylistic hypothesis; never mechanically enforce

evidence_levels.direct_empirical: controlled human-judgment or direct human-vs-AI comparison in academic/medical writing
evidence_levels.direct_corpus_observational: large academic corpus association or drift, not individual-author attribution
evidence_levels.cross_domain_empirical: empirical comparison in other nonfiction genre; transfer uncertain
evidence_levels.research_informed_hypothesis: reasonable editorial concern but AI-specific linkage not established by supplied studies
evidence_levels.policy_invariant: critical preservation/compliance rule; intentionally not an AI-writing indicator

patterns.label: Redundant restatement
patterns.description: Adjacent sentences repeat the same claim without new evidence, distinction, or implication.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Repetition may aid orientation in abstracts or long technical documents; check communicative role.
patterns.editing_guidance: Merge repeated claims; retain the most precise statement and necessary link.

patterns.label: Broken logical thread
patterns.description: Claim-to-evidence progression jumps, or key qualifiers disappear between sentences.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Dense mathematical prose may use separately defined terminology; consult equations and cross-references.
patterns.editing_guidance: Identify premises and evidence; request missing support rather than invent bridges.

patterns.label: Unsupported claims and references
patterns.description: Background or discussion asserts findings without a verifiable source or with fabricated bibliographic details.
patterns.false_positive_guard: General domain definitions may not require citation; journal conventions differ.
patterns.editing_guidance: Verify every substantive referenced claim; mark unverifiable references for author review.

patterns.label: Overstatement of evidence or clinical utility
patterns.description: Wording asserts definitive effects, causal implications, or clinical benefit beyond underlying analysis.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Strong claims are appropriate when design and evidence justify them.
patterns.editing_guidance: Constrain claim to supplied estimand, population, study design, and measurements.

patterns.label: Changed quantitative or methodological facts
patterns.description: Editing changes n, effect size, confidence interval, p-value, comparator, endpoint, method, eligibility, or code identifier.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Formatting normalization is acceptable only if numeric meaning and notation remain equivalent.
patterns.editing_guidance: Block output until source text, tables, and methods match; raise discrepancy.

patterns.label: Generic significance without study-specific stakes
patterns.description: Introduction or grant significance states broad importance without concrete population, gap, or decision relevance.
patterns.false_positive_guard: A general opening can be justified for interdisciplinary audiences.
patterns.editing_guidance: Anchor to supplied burden, gap, mechanism, or research question; do not invent numbers.

patterns.label: Results replaced by evaluative commentary
patterns.description: Abstract or Results paragraphs say findings are promising/important without the measurable result.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Some qualitative research appropriately reports themes rather than effect sizes.
patterns.editing_guidance: Lead with measured results already present in source material; reserve interpretation for Discussion.

patterns.label: Inappropriate rhetorical-move balance
patterns.description: Abstract overweights interpretation, omits context/method or organizes discourse moves unnaturally for target journal.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Structured abstract rules and journal formats override any learned frequencies.
patterns.editing_guidance: Check section function against journal and reporting guidelines; preserve required headings.

patterns.label: Affective/promotional stance imbalance
patterns.description: Positive evaluative language dominates evidence reporting; hedges/boosters lack an evidentiary basis.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Strong recommendations can be justified; standards differ between grants and manuscripts.
patterns.editing_guidance: Replace emotive judgments with evidence-tied interpretation and justified uncertainty.

patterns.label: Generic future work or implications
patterns.description: Conclusion prescribes more research or broad adoption without explaining which uncertainty remains.
patterns.false_positive_guard: A concise future-work statement may be required by a journal or grant.
patterns.editing_guidance: Specify the actual limitation, unanswered question, and relevant next step only if supplied.

patterns.label: Overly symmetric rhetorical framing
patterns.description: Repeated balancing constructions force two-sided treatment where evidence is asymmetric.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Balanced discussion is essential when true uncertainty or conflicting evidence exists.
patterns.editing_guidance: Represent evidentiary balance faithfully, not rhetorically.

patterns.label: Unnecessary metacommentary
patterns.description: Sentences announce what the manuscript will discuss instead of advancing its argument.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Roadmaps are useful in long technical documents; aims and objectives often require explicit signposting.
patterns.editing_guidance: Retain navigation when functional; otherwise replace with the substantive claim.

patterns.label: Overgeneralized comparison with prior work
patterns.description: Prior studies are summarized as uniformly inadequate without concrete contrast in population, design, outcome, or methods.
patterns.false_positive_guard: A synthesis of heterogeneous studies may require broad framing supported by citations.
patterns.editing_guidance: Specify verified comparative dimensions and soften claims unsupported by supplied sources.

patterns.label: LLM-associated lexical clustering and buzzwords
patterns.description: Disproportionate repeated clusters of words reported as LLM-associated or synthetic buzzwords humans rarely choose in scientific prose, such as delve/underscore/pivotal/intricate/testament/beacon/elevate/foster/paramount/tapestry.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Single words are common legitimate English; prevalence varies by year, discipline, and authorship. Never ban or classify from lexical hits.
patterns.editing_guidance: Check whether terms contribute precision; remove ornamental repetition and replace hollow buzzwords with plain, precise scientific language.

patterns.label: Stock emphasis and intensifiers
patterns.description: Terms such as groundbreaking or transformative appear without evidentiary basis.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Innovation sections in grants necessarily argue significance; evaluative terms may be supported.
patterns.editing_guidance: Convert to specific evidence-supported scope or outcome.

patterns.label: Mechanical transition stacking
patterns.description: Successive sentences rely on formulaic transitions despite obvious logical relation.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Transitions can genuinely help complex multi-step reasoning, accessibility, and technical prose.
patterns.editing_guidance: Keep transitions where they encode actual causation/contrast; remove redundant ones.

patterns.label: Uniform sentence construction and low burstiness
patterns.description: Closely repeated syntactic frames, steady metronomic sentence lengths, or uniform clause openings reduce rhythm variation and create a flat, monotonous cadence.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Parallelism is essential in aims, hypotheses, and methods; explicit study design, methodological sequencing, hypothesis enumeration, and reporting conventions override stylistic diversity objectives.
patterns.editing_guidance: Review extended passages for repetitive sentence architecture and monotonous progression; vary structure when doing so improves clarity, emphasis, or argument flow, letting scientific content determine sentence length rather than targeting rigid word counts or statistical distributions.

patterns.label: Unnecessarily abstract nominalizations
patterns.description: Abstract nouns obscure who performed an action or what was measured.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Established statistical and biomedical terms should not be replaced with casual synonyms.
patterns.editing_guidance: Use direct technical verbs when precise, while retaining necessary formal terminology.

patterns.label: Decorative concluding recap
patterns.description: Paragraph ends with a polished but non-informative restatement of broad significance.
patterns.false_positive_guard: A conclusion is legitimately required in most abstracts and papers.
patterns.editing_guidance: Make the concluding sentence answer the specific study question.

patterns.label: Mechanical punctuation habits and em-dash overuse
patterns.description: Heavy and repetitive reliance on em dashes (—) across multiple sentences as parenthetical commentary, theatrical pauses, or clause-stitching crutches; mechanical colon/semicolon stacking.
patterns.false_positive_guard: A single paired em-dash parenthetical within a sentence is standard punctuation; evaluate whether dashes cluster repeatedly across multiple sentences or serve as repetitive rhetorical interruptions.
patterns.editing_guidance: Distinguish legitimate paired parentheticals from repetitive interruptions; replace overused em dashes across sentences with standard syntactic subordination, natural commas, parentheses, or clean sentence splits.

patterns.label: Predictable paragraph architecture and list-like flows
patterns.description: Uniform paragraph lengths across sections, tidy list-like flows, and formulaic summary conclusions at the close of every paragraph.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Explicit study design, methodological sequencing, hypothesis enumeration (such as Specific Aims), and reporting conventions override stylistic diversity objectives.
patterns.editing_guidance: In narrative prose, vary paragraph progression organically; replace tidy formulaic lists with substantive transitions; cut predictable repetitive concluding sentences while preserving functional enumeration in aims, protocols, and methods.

patterns.label: Causality versus association conflation
patterns.description: Observational associations are rewritten as interventions causing changes or as demonstrated mechanisms.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Causal inference designs can support causal language if assumptions and estimand warrant it.
patterns.editing_guidance: Keep causal scope aligned with research design and source claims.

patterns.label: Fabricated specificity
patterns.description: Editor fills in absent sample size, measurement details, computational implementation, references, or preliminary data.
patterns.false_positive_guard: None: unsupported facts must never be supplied as though known.
patterns.editing_guidance: Flag missing information explicitly; do not supply plausible values.

patterns.label: Inconsistent cross-section claims
patterns.description: Abstract, Results, and Discussion describe different populations, endpoints, or effect directions.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Changes may reflect clearly labeled prespecified sensitivity analyses; compare like with like.
patterns.editing_guidance: Check against source-of-truth result tables and primary analysis specification.

patterns.label: Altered authorial scientific judgment
patterns.description: Editing invents research gaps, hypotheses, mechanism claims, aims, or strategic priorities that were not authorized by the author.
patterns.false_positive_guard: Explicit author-approved revisions to substantive plans are permissible outside polishing mode.
patterns.editing_guidance: Preserve the author’s scientific decisions and mark suggestions as questions rather than inserting them.

patterns.label: Ill-fitting authorial presence
patterns.description: Self-mentions, framing statements, or attitude markers do not fit genre and local reporting style.
patterns.false_positive_guard: First person is often recommended and not an AI cue; discipline-specific conventions vary.
patterns.editing_guidance: Adapt only to target journal/discipline; never systematically ban “we”.

S01.title: Doru et al. (2025), Medical student essays and expert AI judgments
S01.notes: Human review; German medical student essays; 69 judgment rounds; redundancy/repetition/coherence associated with identification. Small, domain/language-specific.

S02.title: Russell, Karpinska & Iyyer (ACL 2025), Human identification of AI-written nonfiction
S02.notes: Human review; 300 English nonfiction articles; frequent LLM users rely on lexical cues and higher-level formality, originality, clarity. Not specifically scientific writing.

S03.title: Khera et al. (2025), Scientific writing in the era of LLMs
S03.notes: Expert review; 34 cerebrovascular essays; Stroke editors misclassified 7/22 human-authored essays in majority-based assessment. Small sample.

S04.title: Kobak et al. (Science Advances 2025), Excess vocabulary in biomedical abstracts
S04.notes: Corpus trend; >15 million biomedical abstracts 2010-2024; aggregate excess vocabulary is not proof of authorship.

S05.title: Kousha & Thelwall (Scientometrics 2026), LLM-associated words in full scientific articles
S05.notes: Corpus trend; six scholarly databases and >2.4m PMC full texts; co-occurrence and field variation; cannot distinguish AI-generated vs AI-edited text.

S06.title: Deng, Li & Gao (JEAP 2026), Rhetorical moves and metadiscourse in abstracts
S06.notes: Direct comparison; 120 human/120 ChatGPT applied-linguistics abstracts; results are field/abstract specific.

S07.title: Human-written vs ChatGPT-generated texts: Stance in English research article abstracts (System 2025)
S07.notes: Direct comparison; 600 human and 600 ChatGPT abstracts; AI abstracts more affect-oriented stance. Abstracts only.

S08.title: Park, Jeong & Kim (EMNLP Industry 2026), Style as a Confound
S08.notes: Detector fairness; 135,389 professional editing pairs; detector responses and false positives inconsistent.

S09.title: Davis & Mahmoud (PMLR 2026), Reference hallucinations
S09.notes: Small evaluation; 36 generated academic-style documents; hallucinated references and unsupported claims depend on prompting constraints.

S10.title: NIH (2025), Supporting Fairness and Originality in NIH Research Applications
S10.notes: Funding policy; sections substantially developed by AI not treated as applicant original ideas as of receipt date 2025-09-25.

S11.title: ICMJE (January 2026), AI use by authors
S11.notes: Editorial policy; disclosure, human responsibility, accurate citations and originality.

S12.title: EQUATOR Network, STROBE reporting guideline
S12.notes: Scientific reporting guideline; legitimate methodological conventions must be protected.

S13.title: EQUATOR Network, CONSORT 2025 reporting guideline
S13.notes: Scientific reporting guideline; protect required reporting and trial terminology.

S14.title: Geng & Trotta (Findings ACL 2025), Human-LLM coevolution in academic writing
S14.notes: Corpus trend; some previously AI-associated word rates fell after becoming known; lexical cues drift over time.

S15.title: Zhang & Zhang (JEAP 2025), Disciplinary variation of metadiscourse
S15.notes: Direct comparison across eight disciplines; metadiscourse differences are genre/discipline-dependent.
